column1: # One throwaway git repo per row. `base` files and the driver.json a row names are
# committed, then `ops` runs against the working tree, then the classifier runs
# against the row's run root — the repo root, or the `R:` subdirectory.
# Columns: name  globs  base  ops  expected_stdout  expected_stderr
#   globs  the driver config to commit, one sourceGlobs entry per `|` field:
#            @EMPTY@   write `{}` — a config carrying no sourceGlobs key
#            @SCALAR@  write `{"sourceGlobs":"scripts/**"}` — the key as a JSON
#                      scalar where the schema says array
#   base   files to create and commit at HEAD, `|`-separated, or `-` for none.
#          Every repo also gets a committed README.md seed so HEAD exists.
#   ops    working-tree operations applied after the base commit, `|`-separated,
#            M:<path>  rewrite a tracked file, leave it unstaged
#            E:<path>  rewrite a tracked file and `git add` it
#            S:<path>  create a new file and `git add` it
#            N:<path>  create a new file and leave it untracked
#            R:<dir>   run the classifier against <repo>/<dir> instead of the
#                      repo root, and write the row's driver.json there — a
#                      package subdir carrying its own config. At most one per
#                      row. Every other op path stays relative to the REPO root.
# A reason token naming a path names the FIRST candidate that fires it, and the
# candidate list is `git diff --name-status HEAD` order then
# `git ls-files --others` order — git sorts both by path, so `foo.ps1` always
# precedes `foo.sh`. Rows below expect the .ps1 leg for that reason.
# A non-repo root, a repo with no commits, and a PATH stripped of git or of jq
# have no TSV-expressible shape and ride as bespoke cases at the end of the
# --- deep: a new file under sourceGlobs -----------------------------------
# --- the staged tree, which bare `git diff` cannot see --------------------
# --- rejected path shapes, candidate side and glob side --------------------
# `scripts/a"b.md` arrives from git as `"scripts/a\"b.md"`, a C-quoting that
# `core.quotePath=false` does not suppress. The fixture needs a filesystem that
# permits `"` in a name — which is also why the candidate this row pins cannot
# arise on Windows, where such a name is illegal.
# The floor is applied LAST, so a rejected candidate can only raise a `shallow`
# to `standard`: it never outranks a deep trigger, and it does outrank the bare
# `standard` a matched sourceGlob earns, because it is the one candidate whose
# --- a run root below the git top level -----------------------------------

# untracked file below reads as `scripts/new.md`, matches no glob, and the row
# --- the glob subset: ** crosses /, * and ? do not ------------------------
